 Helm is building the infrastructure layer for world simulation. Physics tools cannot model human behavior. Social AI cannot model physics. Economic tools cannot model either. Helm composes all of them into one platform, so a drought can trigger crop failure, commodity prices can spike, consumer sentiment can shift, and policy can respond, all inside a single pipeline. Teams in defense, reinsurance, energy, and public policy use it to model reality before they bet on it. Every prediction is scored against ground truth, so users know how much to trust the output. The same way containers standardized compute and SQL standardized data, we are building the standard interface for simulation.
 



  





**Role Description** 




 The Software Engineering Apprentice is a full time role for an exceptional early career engineer who wants to learn by shipping into a real production system rather than by working through a curriculum. Early on it is likely to be well defined pieces of the platform: building out the World Library of simulation primitives, writing engine adapters so a new simulation model plugs into the orchestration layer, extending the validation suite that benchmarks runs against historical data, or working on the builder tools that let users configure scenarios and agent populations without writing code. Later it means taking a problem that is still ambiguous and coming back with something that works.
 



  





 You will read a lot of code you did not write. You will ask a lot of questions. * Build and productionize ranking and recommendation models that select and order the best options for a given user request, balancing relevance to the user against business objectives.

* Design and build feature pipelines over behavioral, transactional, and content data, with point\-in\-time correctness so training features match what is available at inference and no label leaks into the model.
* Develop and tune classical ML models (gradient\-boosted trees, linear and logistic models, learning\-to\-rank), and recognize when a simpler model or a rules baseline is the right answer.
